name: Next Greater element to the Right
html:
Welcome back readers!

We hope that you understand the uses of Stack so far. Stacks have a wide range of applications because they make an excellent mechanism for temporary storage of information within procedures.

In this problem we will look at another application of Stack.

Important Links :Question Video

Yes! We will be solving this problem using Stack.

But before moving any further it is advised that you give this problem a try and think of possible ways in which you can solve this.

Let's jump to the problem.

Problem Discussion :

Suppose you are given a number n, representing the size of array a. After that you are given n numbers, representing elements of array a.

You are required to return an array which consists of "next greater element to the right" corresponding to all elements of the array.

Input and output is already handled for you.

"Next greater element on the right" of an element x is defined as the first element to the right of x having value greater than x. Note -> If an element does not have any element on its right side greater than it, consider -1 as it's "next greater element on right"


e.g.

for the array [2 5 9 3 1 12 6 8 7]

Next greater for 2 is 5

Next greater for 5 is 9

Next greater for 9 is 12

Next greater for 3 is 12

Next greater for 1 is 12

Next greater for 12 is -1

Next greater for 6 is 8

Next greater for 8 is -1

Next greater for 7 is -1

You can also watch a question video of this problem to understand WHAT part of the question in a clearer way.

Watch video Approach : What?

First of all, let's understand what needs to be done, in order to collect the answer array.

  • First of all we define an answer array which stores the next greater element at corresponding index to given array, nge[] and a stack st.
  • We traverse the given array in reverse order and push the last element in the stack. And since there is no right element for the last element, we simply store -1 at the last index of the answer array, nge.
  • Now moving to the second last element, we check our stack whether the topmost element is smaller or greater than the present element. If it's smaller than the present element then we pop out those elements of the stack until we get an element which is greater than this. And when we get a greater element we store this element corresponding to the present element in nge and push the present element in our stack.
  • However while popping out smaller elements from our stack, if the stack gets emptied out then we store -1 corresponding to the present element in nge and push the present element in our stack.

If you are still facing any problem regarding the above discussed part then I advise you to watch this part of the solution video.

Watch video How?

Let's try to code this.

  • Defining an answer array nge of the same length of input array arr and a stack st of integer.
  • Then we push last element of arr into st and store -1 at the last index of nge because to the right of last element of arr, there will be no element greater or smaller.
  • Now we run a reverse loop, starting from the second last element of arr.
  • Inside this for loop, first of all we pop out the topmost element until the stack is emptied out or the element in stack is either smaller or equal to the current element of arr.
  • When control comes out of the while loop, it either means that the stack has emptied out or the peek of the stack is greater than the current element (arr[i]).
  • In case if the stack has emptied out then we place -1 at the ith index in nge[] and push the current element (arr[i]) into the stack. Otherwise if the stack is not empty then it means that at the peek of the stack there is a greater element and this needs to be stored at ith index of nge[].
  • At last we simply push the ith value of arr[] into the stack inside the for loop.
  • After we come out of the for loop we simply return nge[]

If you are still facing any problem regarding the above discussed part then I advise you to watch this part of the solution video.

Watch video import java.io.*; import java.util.*; public static int[] solve(int[] arr) { int[] nge = new int[arr.length]; Stack< Integer> st = new Stack< >(); nge[arr.length - 1] = -1; st.push(arr[arr.length - 1]); for(int i = arr.length - 2; i >= 0; i--){ while(st.size() > 0 && arr[i] >= st.peek()){ st.pop(); } if(st.size() == 0){ nge[i] = -1; } else { nge[i] = st.peek(); } st.push(arr[i]); } return nge; }
java; true"; Analysis Time Complexity :

At first it may seem like a while loop is running inside for loop, making the time complexity O(n^2). But this is not the case, the time complexity of this is O(n) only.

Because the while loop inside for loop doesn't run n times. As we are pushing and popping each element of arr[] only once inside the stack.

SPACE COMPLEXITY :

An array of n size is used, making the space complexity O(n).
